blocks.x: Back to school means lots of things—back to routine, back to homework, and, for the parents out there, back to packing school lunches. Perhaps as important as the backpack is the lunch box; unless your kids are only buying lunches, a lunch box is something they’ll use almost every day, so it better hold up to daily wear and tear.

Beyond the lunch box, you also need to think about how your child will transport the food inside. Will you pack everything in baggies and toss those in the lunch box? (If so, we have you covered.) Or, perhaps you want to avoid the waste and handle their need for separated food with an insulated bento box. Whether your kids are 5 or 15, we’ve identified a lunchtime solution. Read on for our top picks for lunch boxes, food storage containers, and related accessories to ensure that school mealtime is a really good time.
Our favorite lunch boxes and containers
AccordionItemContainerButton
Lunch boxes
The most durable: Yeti Daytrip 3L Lunch Box
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/6a9a1f9f054609d32e23d665/3:4/w_748%2Cc_limit/31FuhmhzXSL._SL500_.jpg
blocks.c: Image may contain: First Aid, Baggage, and Suitcase

blocks.x: Yeti
Yeti Daytrip 3L Lunch Box
AccordionItemContainerButton
Pros

• Super durable
• Outside easily wipes off
• Food stays chilled for long periods of time
• Inside storage pouch

Cons
• Bulky
• Ice pack not included
• No room for expansion

It’s probably no surprise that Yeti tops the list in terms of durability. This lunch box is almost like a piece of travel-ready luggage; it cushions the items inside the compartment, so you won’t end up with smashed sandwiches if you’re not using additional containers. (It’s worth noting, though, that Yeti has a nice selection of compatible containers, including one of the best insulated food jars I’ve used.) Its construction does make the Daytrip bulky, so it might not fit in the smaller backpacks early elementary school kids sometimes carry. Also, the lunch box doesn’t expand much, so if you’re packing a bento or containers, you’ll have to find snacks that fit in the bag’s extra-slim interior pouch.

On par with the bag’s top-notch durability is its insulation. Yeti is known for keeping food and drinks well chilled throughout the day, and the Daytrip is no exception. This bag doesn’t come with an ice pack, but any flat one will work—and Yeti does sell its own.

Much like the brand’s water bottles, the Daytrip 3L (and larger 5L) comes in a variety of solid, pop-y colors, so if your kid wants flashy patterns to show off in the cafeteria, you’ll need to look elsewhere.
Cute yet functional: Pack-It Cool Freezable Friends Lunch Box
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/6a9a2da8fe6c31594879b695/3:4/w_748%2Cc_limit/Freezable-Friends-Unicorn-Front-Down-Lores.jpeg
blocks.c: Image may contain: Bag, Accessories, Handbag, Backpack, and Purse

blocks.x: PackIt Cool Freezable Friends Lunch Box
AccordionItemContainerButton
Pros

• No ice pack needed
• Collapsible
• Bag stays cold all day (if stored inside)
• Name tag and optional cross-body strap
• Side mesh pocket and extra front pocket
Cons

• The used lunch box has to go in the freezer
• Not easy to clean exterior
• Pricier than other lunch boxes on the list

When my first child needed a lunch bag for preschool, I started using Pack-It Cool’s Freezable Classic Lunch Box. For me, the selling point is that they don’t need an additional ice pack—you simply squish down the bag and tuck it in the freezer each night—and it truly keeps the food cold all day long. During my kid’s preschool days, any leftover food came home still slightly chilled.

The new Freezable Friends line is the same concept as Pack-It’s original design, but with an adorable upgrade. The line comes in four styles (Unicorn, Fox, Dog, and Truck), and features a removable cross-body strap for Little Miss/Mr. Independents like my daughter, who prefer to haul all their gear solo. It also features a front pouch for extra snacks and a side mesh pocket to hold drinks.

Its greatest asset is also the only thing that bothers me about the bag—the fact that you have to store your child’s bag (and whatever your child touched with it) is on top of your food is, well, a little gross. But if you can get over that, or are OK slipping it inside a zip-top bag before re-freezing, then you’ll love it.
The teenage dream: Stanley Assembly Lunch Box
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/6a9a23922076bf475c8b6003/3:4/w_748%2Cc_limit/31UZIeChr4L._SL500_.jpg
blocks.c: Image may contain: Accessories, Bag, Handbag, First Aid, and Purse

blocks.x: Stanley
Stanley Assembly Lunch Box
AccordionItemContainerButton
Pros

• Lightweight
• Fully insulated
• Coordinates with other Stanley products (water bottles and backpacks)
• Mesh side pouch for water bottle
• Front zip pouch
Cons

• Not a ton of color options
• Not easy to clean exterior
• Ice pack not included

Thanks to their social media ubiquity over the last several years, we’ve seen Stanley water bottles become objects of obsession for teens and tweens, and if that sounds like one of your kids, the brand’s lunch boxes can complete the look. The Stanley Assembly Lunch Box doesn’t have a ton of bells and whistles, but it’s a good, durable lunch box. In my opinion, the size is perfect: It’s not too big and not too small (it holds most of the bento boxes I tried), and its lightweight material keeps it from being clunky. (Even my five-year-old easily lugged it around camp this summer.)

Perhaps the best feature of the Assembly is its side mesh pouch for holding, what else, but a Stanley 1913 (up to 24 oz.). And if your child is full-on Stanley, its buckle clip also pairs with the Assembly Backpack.
One note: While this lunch box is insulated, you’ll need an additional ice pack; a flat one can fit in the lid’s mesh interior pocket.
For full-on coordination: State Bags Rodgers Lunch Box
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/6a9a30484bfb653f5ef9c4ac/3:4/w_748%2Cc_limit/16209823_fpx.jpeg
blocks.c: Image may contain: Accessories, Bag, Handbag, and Purse

blocks.x: State Bags Rodgers Lunch Box
AccordionItemContainerButton
Pros

• Lightweight
• Fully insulated
• Easy to wipe clean
• Thoughtful design elements, including a divider and pocket for notes
• Coordinates with State Bags backpacks
Cons

• Ice pack not included
• When certain styles sell out, they might not be available again

Speaking of coordination, this is the bag my daughter chose on her first day of kindergarten to go along with her State Bag backpack. (I realize you may not be here for backpacks, but this is the only backpack brand I’ve bought my kids during elementary school years because they are so incredibly durable and have thoughtful extra features, like a hidden interior pocket that’s perfect for AirTags.) I’m predicting the same for the lunch box—and so far so good.

Like the Stanley Assembly, the lunch box is both lightweight and the ideal size—it’s large enough to hold my top picks for bento containers. The Rodgers is fully insulated and easy to wipe clean. I love the little details—like the detachable Velcro divider to help keep things organized, and the clear pocket for little notes or pictures. There’s also a zippered interior mesh pocket to hold utensils or other loose items.

Besides all that thoughtfulness around utility, the designs are some of the best out there. Whether your kid is into Hot Wheels or Barbie, or is older and wants something more mature, State Bags has a lunch box look for just about everyone. And, of course, there’s a backpack to go with each style.
Bento boxes
The smartest bento of all: OmieBox Up
